To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a MIMO communication channel can be utilized to stabilize a linear system if and only if the capacities of the SISO channels satisfy a majorization condition.

a necessary and sufficient condition for networked stabilizability via a MIMO transceivers is given by a majorization relation between the capacities of the communication subchannels and the control input weights, and the condition can be checked by the following steps: (1) compute the capacity matrix of the communication subchannel; (2) check the majorization condition; (3) if the condition is satisfied, then design the coding/decoding mechanism and the controller; (4) if the condition fails
the majorization condition is the necessary and sufficient condition for networked stabilizability, and it is a generalization of the well-known water-filling principle in communication theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental issue of networked control systems: how to take advantage of the coding/decoding mechanism for the design of a controller.
a new type of networked control system, in which a MIMO communication channel is introduced between the controller and plant.
a fundamental question: when MIMO control meets MIMO communication, how can the two disciplines benefit each other?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the majorization relation is necessary and sufficient for networked stabilization via MIMO communication, and that the coding/control co- design can be carried out in a systematic manner.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MIMO control theory and MIMO communication theory are indeed complementary to each other.

the coding/control co-desgin is a viable alternative to the traditional controller design in the networked stabilization problem, especially when the number of control inputs is much larger than the number of control outputs.
, when the controller and the communication system are both MIMO, a majorization condition on the capacities can guarantee networked stabilizability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the controller is MIMO and the communication channel is also MIMO, the controller should be able to adapt to the communication resource in order to stabilize the networked plant.

, in order for the MIMO communication scheme to be effective in networked stabilization, it is necessary to impose some constraints on the capacities of subchannels, which is in sharp contrast to the traditional MIMO communication problem.
